hypotheses.reasoning: At 09:52:11Z notif-db reloaded the notifications table from a snapshot (2,186,750 rows), but AUTO_INCREMENT was left at 2,167,241, about 19.5k IDs behind the real max id. From 09:53:06Z onward, inserts that reuse IDs already in the table fail with Duplicate entry on notifications.PRIMARY (#180, #195, #205, #211). notification-svc turns these into 409 unique-violation/500 create failures (#186), and api-gateway surfaces them as POST /v1/notify 500s (#189), which is the alert. Before the restore the service was healthy (e.g. #156-#173 all 200). The gateway 5xx and the 409s are downstream symptoms. The audit_log slow query (#66), the InnoDB flush lines, and template-svc and redis, which show no errors, are not causal. The restore is the origin; the AUTO_INCREMENT counter was not advanced afterward.

The restore runbook's post-restore step (resetting AUTO_INCREMENT to max(id)+1) may have been skipped or misconfigured. This is an alternative reading of the same line, but the fault itself is the stale counter, so data_integrity is the better fit.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately set the notifications AUTO_INCREMENT on notif-db to max(id)+1 (at least 2186751) so inserts stop colliding. Verify that the restore did not lose or duplicate data by comparing the snapshot with notifications written since. Add a post-restore check that compares AUTO_INCREMENT with MAX(id) before traffic is re-enabled. Replay the rejected POST /v1/notify requests from the window, since they failed rather than saved.
